answer: I'd like to talk about the device I'd miss most if it suddenly disappeared. A device I would genuinely struggle to live without is my mobile phone, which has become [[deeply woven into]] every part of my day. I rely on it for communication, work, navigation, banking and entertainment, all in one place. In the morning it wakes me up, at work I use it to answer students' questions and track application deadlines, and in the evening I video-call my elder sister in Dhaka so my parents can chat with their grandchildren. I also pay most of my bills through a mobile banking app. What makes it so [[indispensable]] is the sheer number of tasks it handles that once required separate tools. It is not just the convenience but the fact that so much of my daily life is organised through it. Most of my contacts, work files and appointments exist only on that phone. I am aware this level of [[dependence]] is not entirely healthy, and I do sometimes worry about it. Honestly, if I lost it, I think I would feel quite [[disoriented]], at least for the first few days. If I had to cope without it, I imagine I would eventually adapt, as people did for generations before. I'd probably go back to writing things down in a notebook, keeping important numbers on paper and visiting people in person more often, which might not be such a bad thing. Still, in the short term it would be genuinely [[disruptive]]. It is a striking reminder of how quickly these devices have become essential rather than optional in modern life.

followUps.q: Have you ever tried a day without your phone?
followUps.answer: Once, during a visit to my grandparents' village, where the signal was very weak. It was frustrating at first, but by the evening it felt surprisingly [[liberating]] to simply sit and talk.

followUps.q: Do your parents rely on their phones as much?
followUps.answer: Not nearly as much. My father mainly uses his for calls and the news, and my mother uses hers to video-call my elder sister. They're far less attached than my generation.

note: Reordered so 'why you rely on it' precedes 'how you would cope'; added daily uses (work, family video calls, bills) and a concrete coping plan; new mark 'deeply woven into'.
